subject: Insurance
title: The Actuarial Revolution
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Actuarial Revolution.

hook.text: In 1693, Edmond Halley built the first mortality table.

buildup.text: Before Halley, insurers guessed premiums. Some charged too much; others went bankrupt from charging too little.

discovery.text: Mortality tables turned guessing into science. Insurers could now price life insurance based on actual death rates.

twist.text: Halley's table used records from Breslau, Germany—a city chosen because its population was unusually stable.

climax.text: Actuarial science made insurance profitable and fair. Math replaced intuition, and the modern industry was born.

punchline.text: Halley mapped death by age. Math made insurance a real industry.

quiz.question: What did Edmond Halley create in 1693?
